name: Hollow cheeks via chewing then fat loss

lead: This approach pairs masseter-focused chewing with body and facial fat loss to bring out the cheekbones and the hollow below them. The goal is hollow cheeks with a more visible cheekbone and jaw.

Proponents describe the hollow as coming from cheekbone projection, jaw angle and masseter size, which become visible when facial fat is low. Wikipedia notes the buccal fat pad also contributes to cheek fullness. No clinical study of the combination was found, and forum members disagree about the look itself.

paras: People chew firm gum or tough foods to work the masseter while reducing body fat through diet and training over weeks to months, and track the cheeks and jaw in photos taken in consistent lighting.
No harms were documented for the combination in the sources reviewed. Medical literature associates very hollow cheeks with aging or lipodystrophy, conditions treated with volume restoration.

angle.text: Forum posters build the masseter with chewing and lower body and facial fat so cheekbones and jaw structure show more, creating hollow cheeks. They describe the hollow as coming from bone and muscle, revealed by less soft tissue. No studies test the combination.

lead: "Hollow cheeks via chewing then fat loss" refers to a looksmaxxing approach that combines masseter-focused chewing with reducing body and facial fat, in order to show cheekbone and jaw structure. Proponents describe hollow cheeks as the shadowed area below the cheekbones, produced by bone, muscle and the amount of soft tissue.

No published trial was found that tests chewing followed by fat loss for cheek hollowing. Medical literature in this area concerns facial fat loss from aging and lipodystrophy, and treatments such as fillers and fat grafting to restore cheek volume [1][2][3][4]. Wikipedia notes the buccal fat pad contributes to cheek hollowing, but it describes no chewing-based method [5].

paras: Looksmax.org members describe two broad sources of hollow cheeks: those formed by zygomatic bone projection and those formed by the masseter muscle and jaw angle, with lighting changing how pronounced they appear. In threads on the topic, members also point to a low level of facial fat as a precondition, and some ask whether hollow cheeks can be achieved without dieting.
Others dispute the goal. One thread argues hollow cheeks can look overly gaunt and that cheek dimples with a thin fat layer look better.

No studies found. Related medical literature is about restoring lost cheek volume: reports on microliposuction and fat transplantation in the aging face [1], collagen fillers used to augment hollow cheeks [2], reconstruction in partial lipodystrophy where extremely hollow cheeks are a feature [3], and a corrective surgery for hollow cheeks [4]. These address volume replacement, not chewing or deliberate fat loss.

Wikipedia describes the buccal fat pad as a deep cheek fat mass that contributes to hollow cheeks and the nasolabial fold, but not to jowls [5]. It lists proposed roles in suckling and as a gliding pad for chewing muscles [5]. It does not discuss whether chewing changes cheek shape.

lore.intro: Hollow cheeks are a frequent topic on looksmax.org, with members describing multiple routes to them and disagreeing about how desirable they are.

claims.claim: Hollow cheeks come from bone and masseter structure, with fat loss revealing them.
Overly hollow cheeks can look gaunt, and a thin fat layer may be preferable.
